claims.statement: Smaller PV systems can be too individually small for traditional O&M economics, experience fragmented service and delayed repairs, and benefit from portfolio bundling.
PVGIS supplies free irradiance and expected-performance data suitable for a first-pass baseline, but it does not establish equipment fault or contractual liability.
PV degradation and failure have multiple technology-specific mechanisms, requiring component-aware investigation rather than output-only diagnosis.
Poland had 21,225 MW of PV capacity in 2024, proving a large installed base but not the count of addressable commercial rooftop portfolios.

At least one major module warranty requires prompt notice, detailed identifiers, purchase evidence, photos or test reports, and potentially independent laboratory testing, which creates an evidence-assembly job.
Polish commercial counterparties may contractually limit or exclude statutory warranty liability, so the desk must screen actual contracts before modelling recovery.
Free manufacturer monitoring and Polish plans from 49 PLN net monthly that include warranty handling are direct substitutes for monitoring-led positioning.
Published Polish service prices for up-to-50-kWp systems range from 59 to 279 PLN net monthly, with a 2,299 PLN net one-off inspection; larger systems are quote-only.
PV curtailment was material in Poland in 2024, so dispatch and grid constraints can produce low measured output unrelated to a warranty defect.
Vendor API availability and accuracy are not guaranteed, increasing integration and evidentiary risk for a multi-vendor telemetry service.
The median Polish recovery amount, acceptance probability, resolution time, and conversion rate for a paid evidence desk are not established by the reviewed sources.

contrary_evidence: Low-cost and free monitoring products already include alerting and, in some cases, warranty administration.
Commercial contractual exclusions can eliminate otherwise plausible statutory claims.
Curtailment and ordinary performance factors can mimic equipment underperformance.
Manufacturer claim procedures can shift testing cost back to the claimant when breach is not confirmed.
Vendor telemetry access is revocable or unstable and can make supposedly scalable onboarding bespoke.
